auth_type.correction: appToken (optional identification for public SODA 2.1 reads); Socrata API keys are separate key-and-secret authentication credentials

rate_limits.correction: Anonymous SODA 2.1 requests use a shared IP-based pool and may be throttled at an unspecified threshold. App-token requests are currently not throttled unless abusive or malicious; there is no published numeric higher quota.

cors.correction: yes; Socrata supports CORS for read-only access to public datasets

description.correction: City of Los Angeles datasets are available through Socrata SODA. The listed /resource endpoint is the fully supported SODA 2.1 API, where public reads may be anonymous and an optional app token provides a separate request pool. SODA3 is now the platform default and generally requires an app token or authenticated identity for queries.

notes: The legacy SODA 2.1 endpoint is live and remains officially supported, although SODA3 is now the default. The example dataset is historical: LAPD stopped updating it after moving to NIBRS datasets. The clearest errors are conflating app tokens with API keys, claiming published higher limits, and leaving CORS unknown.
